title: WPSS/623/2026 of ANKIT KUMAR Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
2026:UHC:4394
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT
NAINITAL
HON'BLE SRI JUSTICE MANOJ KUMAR TIWARI
Writ Petition No. 623 of 2026 (SS)
Ankit Kumar -- Petitioner
Versus
State of Uttarakhand and others -- Respondents
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Advocates: Mr. Ankit Kumar, petitioner in person
Mr. K.N. Joshi, Deputy Advocate General for the State
Ms. Priyanka Agrawal, Advocate for Selecting Body
Mr. Prateek Tripathi, Advocate for respondent No. 3
----------------------------------------------------------------------
JUDGMENT
1. Petitioner participated in a selection for
appointment to the post of 'Forester', held by
Uttarakhand Subordinate Service Selection Commission
(UKSSSC). Since petitioner was declared unsuccessful
in the selection, therefore he has approached this Court
seeking the following reliefs:
i. Issue a writ of order or direction in the nature of certiorari
quashing the arbitrary appointment of respondent no.3 vide the
recommendation list dated 24.12.2025 and Notice/Letter dated
03.02.2025. (ANNEXURE NO.1&2)
ii. Issue a writ of order or direction in the nature of mandamus
directing the respondent authorities to assess the vacancies in
accordance with the updated roaster in compliance with the GO
dated 22.05.2020.
iii. Issue a writ of order or direction in the nature of mandamus
directing the respondent authorities to decide the
representation of the petitioner given to Uttarakhand through
Secretary, Uttarahand Subordinate Service Selection
Commission (UKSSSC) and Chief Conservator of Forests,
Human Resource Development and Personnel Management,
Dehradun, Uttarakhand expeditiously.
iv. Issue a writ of order or direction in the nature of mandamus
directing the respondent authorities to consider the petitioner
for the post of Forester after assessment of vacancies in
compliance with the GO dated 22.05.2020.
2. The sole contention raised by the petitioner
against appointment of respondent No. 3 is that even
1

2026:UHC:4394
though respondent No. 3 had not submitted hill
certificate with his online application in response to the
advertisement, respondent No. 3 was given benefit of
relaxed standard regarding height, which was available
to candidates having hill certificate.
3. It is not in dispute that respondent No. 3 did not
upload hill certificate with his online application and hill
certificate was issued to respondent No. 3 only on
26.11.2025, while the last date for submission of online
application for appointment was 28.02.2025.
4. As per the advertisement, every male candidate
should be not less than 163 cm in height; however, for
candidate belonging to Scheduled Tribes, Gorkha,
Nepali, Assami, Ladakhi, Sikkim, Bhutan, Garhwal,
Kumaoni, Naga and Arunanchal Pradesh, Lahaul & Spiti,
and Meghalaya communities, the standard regarding
height was relaxed to 152 cm. However, in the
advertisement, it was clearly indicated that benefit of
relaxed standard regarding height would be available to
candidates who produced hill certificate with their
application form.
5. Ms. Priyanka Agarwal, learned counsel appearing
for Selecting Body, submits that height of respondent
No. 3, as per his application form, is 164 cm; however,
during measurement after selection, his height was
found to be 160 cm, which is much less than what is
required.
6. She submits that since respondent No. 3 produced
hill certificate at the time of document verification,
2

2026:UHC:4394
therefore respondent No. 3 was given benefit, which is
available to hill candidates.
7. Learned counsel appearing for respondent No. 3
concedes that his client was not having hill certificate at
the time of submission of online application in response
to the advertisement issued by Selecting Body and hill
certificate was issued to respondent No. 3 after
commencement of selection process and said certificate
was produced before Selecting Body at the time of
document verification.
8. It is contended on behalf of Selecting Body and
also respondent No. 3 that there is nothing wrong in
giving benefit available to candidates belonging to Hills
to respondent No. 3, as he possesses hill certificate
issued by the competent authority.
9. The petitioner, however, contends that since
respondent No. 3 was not having hill certificate on the
last date of submission of application and further,
respondent No. 3 did not enclose/upload hill certificate
with his application to the Selecting Body, therefore he
is not entitled to the benefit available to hill candidates,
especially when hill certificate was issued for the first
time in favour of respondent No. 3, only on
26.11.2025.
10. This Court finds substance in the submission made
by petitioner.
11. Respondent No. 3 was not meeting the eligibility
condition as regards height mentioned in the
advertisement. The online application submitted by him
3

2026:UHC:4394
is enclosed with the supplementary affidavit dated
18.05.2026 filed by Mr. Nandan Singh Dungariyal,
Secretary, Uttarakhand Subordinate Service Selection
Commission. Perusal of online application reveals that
respondent No. 3 mentioned his height as 164 cm.
12. Learned counsel appearing for Selecting Body
submits that height of respondent No. 3 was found to
be 160 cm only and due to incorrect information
furnished by him, he was permitted to participate in the
selection, as the Selecting Body had no mechanism
available to determine height of a candidate before
declaration of result of written examination.
13. Having regard to the facts and circumstances of
the case, this Court has no hesitation in holding that
respondent No. 3 was not eligible to be recommended
for appointment against a post reserved for hill
candidate, when he obtained hill certificate much after
last date of submission of online application. Every
candidate who desires to claim a benefit which is
available to a particular category has to submit
supporting certificate declaring him to belong to that
particular category, with his application form and he
should also indicate in the application that he is
claiming such benefit in the selection.
14. In the absence of any stipulation to the contrary in
the advertisement, every candidate interested in
claiming benefit available to candidates belonging to a
special category must possess certificate, indicating
that he belongs to such special category, on or before
the last date of submission of application and he must
4

2026:UHC:4394
submit such certificate with his application before the
Selecting Body. Since respondent No. 3 was not having
hill certificate on the last date and such certificate was
issued in his favour much after declaration of result of
written examination, therefore such certificate could
not have been relied upon by the Selecting Body for
giving some benefit to respondent No. 3, which was
available only to candidates belonging to hills.
15. In such view of the matter, recommendation made
by Selecting Body in favour of respondent No. 3 is
liable to be set aside and is hereby set aside.
16. Writ petition is allowed. The vacancy which would
arise on the post of Forester on account of this
determination, shall be filled by picking up a candidate
belonging to appropriate category from the waiting list,
as per merit.
17. Petitioner contends that he has also challenged
the requisition sent by State Government to Selecting
Body. After unconditionally participating in the
selection, which was held strictly as per requisition,
petitioner cannot be permitted to question the
requisition. In other words, petitioner is estopped from
challenging the requisition at this belated stage.
18. The prayer made in that regard is, therefore,
rejected.
_______________________________
MANOJ KUMAR TIWARI, J.
Dt: 02.06.2026
